- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap forecast decline to 5–10% below peak unless sentiment shifts.
- Model consistently underestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67); add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00/0.33 values, model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 1–2 prior-day closing price if no clear trend.
- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over 3–5 days, model overestimates; apply 1–3% downward correction to avoid overshoot.
- If model forecast exceeds true outcome by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, apply “mean reversion” rule: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.
